stem: Which condition is characterized by the superior oblique muscle being unable to pass freely through the trochlea?
explanation: Brown syndrome is a restrictive condition where the eye fails to elevate properly when looking inward due to a trochlear impediment.
rationale: This syndrome is named after the person who described the mechanical restriction of the superior oblique tendon.

optionExplanations.A: Brown syndrome is a restrictive condition where the eye fails to elevate properly when looking inward due to a trochlear impediment.
optionExplanations.B: Dwayne syndrome is caused by abnormal innervation of the lateral rectus muscle, not a mechanical trochlear issue.
optionExplanations.C: Third nerve palsy is a paralytic condition involving nerve damage, whereas Brown syndrome is restrictive.
optionExplanations.D: This is a form of early-onset constant misalignment, not a restrictive tendon problem.
